mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for two consecutive weeks (-48.9 to -41.9), indicating positive momentum in recovering foot traffic. This momentum is expected to persist, pushing the next-4-week mean above the last-4-week mean.
failure_condition: Next-4-week mean RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than last-4-week mean despite the prior two weeks showing consecutive increases.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -40 percent-from-baseline for two consecutive weeks, it signals restored commuting and errand trips that mechanically feed retail and recreation visits within 2 weeks, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -40 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -47.9 to -39.7 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 2 weeks after TRANSIT sustains above -40 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility interacts to compound retail footfall gains: commuters returning to offices both travel more and make more incidental retail stops, amplifying RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over 4 weeks is no larger than the growth predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, indicating no compounding interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: In an easing-restrictions regime, a sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 11.4 to 10.0) reflects reduced home-bound behavior, indicating households are substituting stay-at-home time with out-of-home retail and recreation activity over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 11.4 to 10.0 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks even though RESIDENTIAL continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in PARKS (-24.3 to -7.0) reflects warm June weather drawing people to outdoor recreation instead of indoor retail venues, causing a substitution effect that suppresses RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -24.3 at t-2w to -7.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks concurrently with continued strong PARKS growth, contradicting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM mobility near its least-negative level in the series (-14.4) signals the lifting of movement restrictions on essential-adjacent trips, which typically precedes broader relaxation enabling discretionary retail and recreation visits to rise within 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -22.9 to -14.4 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 4 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining at or above -14.4.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL drops below 10.0 week-on-week, indicating a decisive behavioral shift away from home confinement, RETAIL_REC is expected to jump upward within the following week as pent-up discretionary trips are released.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is at 10.0 at t-0w, down from 10.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 1 week after RESIDENTIAL crosses below 10.0.

mechanism_narrative: The large week-to-week volatility in PARKS (swinging from -7.7 to -24.3 to -7.0) reflects an unstable, event-driven pattern (e.g., weather or holiday effects) rather than a durable trend; this instability signals that recent RETAIL_REC gains are similarly noise-driven and will mean-revert, leaving the next 4-week mean flat to lower relative to the last 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung by more than 15 points in consecutive weeks (t-3w to t-2w and t-2w to t-1w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise steadily over the next 4 weeks without reverting, despite high PARKS volatility in the snapshot.
